{{Quote|Essence transfer is the secret of eternal life. The physical body will always weaken and fail, yet it is nothing but a shell or vessel. When it is time, it is possible to transfer your consciousness&mdash;your spirit&mdash;into a new vessel&hellip;|[[Darth Andeddu]]|<ref name="DOE" />}}
'''Essence transfer''', also known as '''transfer essence ''', '''transfer life''', '''transference''', '''reincarnation''', or '''spirit transference''', was a [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[The Force/Legends|Force]] [[Force power/Legends|power]] used to transfer a person's consciousness into another body, or in some cases an inanimate object. Ancient [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] and other powerful darksiders used this technique to cheat death again and again, haunting their tombs and possessing those who stumbled across their sarcophagi in order to continue their reign of terror. In more recent eras, masters of this dark side art had used advanced [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] technology to assure their immortality.

==Description==
{{Quote|The ritual is fraught with danger. Attempting it will cause the current vessel to be destroyed; your body will be consumed by the power of the dark side.|Darth Andeddu|<ref name="DOE" />}}
[[File:Transfer_in_clone_body_BoS.jpg|thumb|left|270px|A schematic representation of essence transfer]]
The power enabled the wielder's spirit to survive the death of their organic body by usurping control of a suitable receptacle. If the invading consciousness was powerful enough, it could override and destroy the mind of the target body. However, it was nearly impossible to overcome a spirit already residing in a body, and moreover the practitioner's own body would disintegrate when the power was invoked. If the target successfully resisted the possession attempt, the practitioner's [[Force ghost/Legends|disembodied spirit]], with nowhere else to go, was consigned to [[Chaos/Legends|Chaos]].<ref name="DESB" /> Given the power's inherent difficulty, its unpredictable nature, and the unspeakable consequences of failure, [[Set Harth]] and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] chose to have their bodies cloned by trained technicians and kept in a hidden safe-house, unconscious in stasis tanks until they were needed. The clones, lacking life experiences or a sense of self, were each little more than a blank slate, upon which the original could imprint their consciousness with ease.<ref name="UA">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref><ref name="Dark Empire endnotes">[[Dark Empire endnotes|''Dark Empire'' endnotes]]</ref>

==Users==
{{Quote|The dying is painful. The transition is not an enjoyable experience. But it is all a small price to pay&hellip;for eternal life.|Palpatine|<ref name="DE2" />}}
Among the earliest Sith Lords to use this technique was [[Karness Muur]], a Lord of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], who bound his spirit to the [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith artifact]] that bore his name, the [[Muur Talisman]]. The talisman allowed Muur not only to cheat death, but also to take possession of whoever wore the Talisman, unless the wearer's willpower was strong enough to resist him, as was the case with [[Celeste Morne]].<ref name="V">''[[Star Wars: Vector]]''</ref>

At some point after the [[Discovery of Korriban]],<ref name="Dark Lord">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}} says that the tite "Dark Lord of the Sith" began to be used after the Discovery of Korriban.</ref> the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]<ref name="Legacy 5">[[Legacy (2006) 5|''Legacy'' (2006) 5]]</ref> [[Darth Andeddu]] used essence transfer to live for centuries.<ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref>

The [[Sith Emperor/Legends|Sith Emperor]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] was one of history's most powerful practitioners of this art. Not only did he reign for over 1000 years using a multitude of different bodies he called [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|Emperor's Voice]], he also imparted some of his essence into several hundred, maybe thousand individuals he called his [[Children of the Emperor]]. His skill in this power was so great that he could continuously exist without a host without succumbing to chaos or madness, could inhabit a host's mind without displacing the original personality for extended periods of time, and even maintain complete [[Ziost/Legends|control over several thousand bodies at once]].<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Voice of the Emperor (Warrior)}}</ref> Unlike Palpatine, Vitiate seems to have been able to limit the amount of premature degeneration which would usually be caused by powerful dark side energy, to the point where his [[Valkorion|last known body]] seems to have aged at the same rate as an ordinary human with little to no dark side degeneration. This might have been caused by Vitiate using the bodies of individuals already powerful with the Force, while Palpatine used empty clone bodies.

Unlike his spiritual descendants, [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], the Dark Lord of the Sith who instigated the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], used this power not to suborn another body but to anchor his spirit<ref name="DSS" /> to the [[Massassi Temple (disambiguation)|Massassi Temples]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. When his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] betrayed him to the Jedi, Kun called all of his [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] followers into the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]], then used their life force to abandon his body and anchor his spirit to the physical world.<ref name="DLOTS6">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 6|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 6]]</ref> Kun's spirit remained on Yavin 4 for over four thousand years,<ref name="Dark Apprentice">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref> driven mad by the unthinkable isolation.<ref name="characters" /> His spirit was finally vanquished by the students at Luke Skywalker's [[Jedi Praxeum|Jedi academy]], [[11 ABY/Legends|seven years]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="Champions of the Force">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref>

In [[3643 BBY]], [[Darth Zash]] attempted to use this power on her apprentice, [[Darth Nox|Kallig]]. Zash had spent years searching for relics of the ancient Sith Lord [[Tulak Hord]] to aid her in the ritual, but was foiled when the [[Dashade/Legends|Dashade]] [[Khem Val]] interceded to protect his master Kallig. Instead of stealing her powerful apprentice's body, she was inadvertently trapped in Khem Val's body with both of their consciousnesses vying for control. The battle ultimately ended when Zash was removed and placed in a [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Mind prison]].

In [[980 BBY]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], fearing that he would die before his apprentice, [[Darth Zannah]], was ready to succeed him as Dark Lord of the Sith, sought to learn the power of essence transfer. His [[Mission to Prakith (Darth Bane)|quest]] led him to [[Prakith/Legends|Prakith]], where [[Andeddu's Keep|Darth Andeddu's keep]] was located. While there, Bane acquired [[Holocron of Heresies|Darth Andeddu's holocron]] by plundering it from the [[Malevolence (cult)|cult that worshiped him]]. The gatekeeper of the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] refused to teach the power of essence transfer to Darth Bane, so Bane decided to rip the information out of the holocron, absorbing it directly into his mind. He later attempted to transfer his essence into Darth Zannah during [[Duel on Ambria (980 BBY)|their final duel]], an act that burned his body to nothing as his spirit shed it,<ref name="DOE" /> but her willpower was strong enough to repel the invasion, thus proving her worth to carry on Darth Bane's legacy. However, some of Darth Bane's manner still lingered within Zannah, stamping her with some of his physical tics.<ref name="Dark">{{WebCite|url=http://www.drewkarpyshyn.com/spoiler.htm|text=Karpyshyn explains the outcome of Dynasty of Evil on his website|archivedate=20230102174043}}</ref><ref name="DOE" />

Set Harth, a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] from the era of the [[New Sith Wars]], learned this technique from Darth Andeddu's holocron after taking it from the [[Stone Prison]] on [[Doan]];<ref name="DOE" /> he used the power to shuttle his consciousness through a series of cloned bodies in much the same manner as Palpatine, nearly a millennium later. However, Set Harth's clones were provided by discreet third-party technicians, and never displayed degradation of the kind Palpatine experienced. Nevertheless, Harth tended to discard them around their 30th year. Using these methods, he was able to survive until at least the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|Yuuzhan Vong Invasion]] and possibly beyond, therefore he must have gone through dozens of clones over the intervening centuries.<ref name="UA" />

[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] was aware of the concept of essence transfer. However, he deliberately avoided using it, as he intended to maintain his own body in complete immortality. Unfortunately for Plagueis, he ultimately never discovered a way to cheat death before his assassination at Palpatine's hands in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> In his notes he did admit that if he could do so, he would have in preference to full death.<ref>[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side|''Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side'']]</ref>

[[Cronal]] also became aware of this ability after intense study of various dark side sites as well as knowledge Palpatine imparted on him. However, he had no intention of using the ability to transfer his mind to a clone but rather use it to take over a living sentient body through [[Pawn]]s. He later attempted to accomplish this feat in order to place his mind in [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] at the [[Battle of Mindor]].<ref name="Mindor">''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]''</ref>

[[File:Last_Clone_Body.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Palpatine attempting to essence transfer into [[Anakin Solo]].]]
Emperor Palpatine was the most prolific practitioner of this esoteric technique in the modern era, surviving<ref name="DE2" /><ref name="DEII">[[Dark Empire II 1|''Dark Empire II'' 1]]</ref> his first death<ref name="DHBoards">{{DHBoards|url=viewtopic.php?p=101353&highlight=#101353|thread=Dark Empire does NOT need a rewrite because of ROTS|user=[[Leland Chee]]|date=2005-05-26|time=06:39|quote=None of the versions of Palpatine that you see in the films is a clone.}}</ref> at the hands of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>
and another at the hands of Anakin's children<ref name="DE6">[[Dark Empire 6|''Dark Empire'' 6]]</ref> by transferring his spirit into fresh clone bodies.<ref name="DE2" /><ref name="DEII" />However, Palpatine's strength in the dark side of the Force caused each clone to degenerate at an accelerated rate,<ref name="Dark Empire endnotes" /> forcing him to take new clone bodies periodically.<ref name="DE2" /> The clones' rate of degeneration was increased further by [[Emperor's physician|sabotage]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Additionally, he used this power to [[Torture/Legends|torture]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]] after the destruction of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|first Death Star]], and during perceived lack of progress on developing the [[Death Star II/Legends|second]]. In total, Lemelisk was killed painfully and resurrected seven times; via such means as being dropped into a vat of molten metal; usually when one of the Imperial engineer's [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] designs failed. Each time, Lemelisk died in agony, only to awaken in a fresh clone. His reaction to being captured, when faced with execution by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], was to simply say, "If you're going to execute me, just make sure you do it right this time."<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref>

The [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] crime lord [[Durga Besadii Tai]] claimed to know essence transfer and implied that he'd use it on Lemelisk should he fail on the Darksaber. However, Lemelisk wasn't sure if this was true, or even if he was skilled at it to Palpatine's level, fearing that the result would be botched.<ref name="Darksaber" />

Perhaps the most unusual examples of this technique in practice occurred in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], and again in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], when Jedi Knight [[Callista Ming]] made use of the power to transfer her soul into the mainframe of the Imperial battlestation ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]''. She was able to "inhabit" the gunnery computer of the dreadnought for some three decades before swapping her essence with the willing [[Cray Mingla]], although this came at the cost of her ability to use the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]].<ref name="COTJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>

This incident differs from nearly all other reported examples of spirit transference in several ways. First, Callista was able to use this predominantly dark side ability, usually applied by powerful Sith Lords, to transfer her consciousness into an inanimate object, despite her commitment to the light side of the Force. Nor did she require alchemical apparatus or additional life energy. Second, rather than becoming a disembodied shade, Callista became part of the ''Eye''{{'s}} gunnery mainframe, acting more like a self-aware computer program than a manifest presence. Thirdly, once she transferred her spirit into the body of Jedi trainee Cray Mingla, she could only touch the dark side of the Force. This was unusual, since both Callista and Cray were Force-sensitive. Since she remained committed to the Jedi way (even going so far as to help Luke Skywalker train new Jedi at the Yavin IV academy), she was essentially cut off from the Force, unlike Palpatine, Set Harth, or Exar Kun.<ref name="Darksaber" /> As none of the Sith had any compunctions about using the dark side, this "handicap", if they possessed it, was essentially meaningless.

The dark side entity [[Abeloth]] utilized essence transfer, whereby she took control of various people and made them avatar bodies for herself.<ref name="FOTJ">''[[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[Dark Empire 5|''Dark Empire'' 5]] mentions Luke "realizing the Emperor can only transfer his consciousness to a living body",<ref name="DE5" /> but the ''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]'' says that it's easier to essence transfer into a "recently dead body" than into a living person.<ref name="DESB" />

Before being updated to be useful when a player was slain in the Saga ruleset<ref name="Jedi Academy Training Manual">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> in the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]], this ability was represented by the skill Transfer Essence. Unlike the ability described above (such as in the example of Palpatine), the Transfer Essence skill required the player to make a conscious effort while still living and had a maximum range of 10 meters. Furthermore, a target who successfully resisted possession was forevermore immune to further attempts by that character. Activating the ability was extremely taxing, and if the first few attempts failed, the character's consciousness was dragged screaming into the yawning abyss of Chaos. Even if they successfully usurped control of another character, that character had a chance to reassert itself whenever the possessor called particularly heavily on the Force.<ref name="DSS" /> The ability exemplified by Palpatine, however, had no range limit and functioned even if death caught Palpatine by surprise, as it did aboard the [[Eclipse (Eclipse-class)|''Eclipse'']].<ref name="DE6" /><ref name="DEII" />

The object transfer version of the skill required that the player also have ranks in the Alchemy skill (the in-game representation of the dark art of [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]]) and expend the life force of other willing beings in order to power the transfer (as with Exar Kun and the Massassi). To take ranks in either Transfer Essence or Alchemy, the player had to possess the [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith Sorcery]] feat, which allowed the player to [[Invoke spirits|call upon the spirits of long-dead Sith Lords]] to improve their offensive and defensive capabilities as well as their skill with the dark side of the Force. However, the ability lasted only for a short time, and each use allowed the Sith Lords a chance to escape their imprisonment in Chaos by possessing the player character.<ref name="DSS" />
